newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/8 to 1/4 pt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/8 to 1/4 pt.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices ended Tuesday's quiet session 1/8 to 1/4 point higher, trailing gains by U.S. Treasuries.
"Treasuries are up 3/8 and we are up 1/4, so we lagged a little bit because we outperformed for so long," one municipal trader said.

The trader added that municipals are trading at tight ratios to U.S. Treasuries. Delphis Hanover Corp figures showed 30-year triple-A municipals yielding 80.9 percent of comparable Treasuries at Tuesday's close. That ratio hit its lowest level in more than two years on May 28.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond Tuesday ended up 12/32 at 96-29/32 to yield 6.87 percent. The bond was helped by technical factors and building sentiment that the economy will slow in the second quarter.
Back in muni cash, an analyst judged the overall market up 1/8 to 1/4 point. High-grade issues improved by two basis points overall, with more improvement seen through five years.
Dollar bonds, which had been up 1/8 point at noon, ended 1/8 to 1/4 point higher, the analyst said.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract ended up 13/32 at 115-29/32. The September T-bond contract closed up 11/32 at 110-3/32. The MOB spread was 186 ticks.
Turning to new issues, the analyst described new issue pricing as "firm to strong" overall.
In competitive action, Bear Stearns & Co won $200 million New York City fiscal 1997 Series M GOs at a true interest cost of 5.73 percent.
Also Tuesday, Lehman Brothers won $150 million of Virginia general obligation bonds with a true interest cost of 5.0963 percent.
On the negotiated side, Merrill Lynch & Co priced $93.75 million New York State Dormitory Authority bonds at a top yield of 5.75 percent in 2037.
Reuters said Tuesday it calculated its 30-day visible supply of upcoming municipal bond sales at $4.964 billion.
Negotiated sales total $2.722 billion and competitive bond sales total $2.242 billion.
